target_customer: Banks, fintechs, funds, brokers, insurers and payments companies with large event datasets
problem: Hand-engineered features miss patterns across transaction histories; institutions want better fraud, credit and churn predictions without sending data outside their cloud.
business_model: Custom private foundation model development and deployment per institution plus software to keep it current
product_category: Enterprise foundation models on event and transaction data

founders.name: Gabriel Noya
education: Stanford, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, class of 2026 (YC bio)

founders.name: Markus Höhn
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page only; no other source mentioned him.

competitors.name: Plaid sequential foundation model
competitors.what: Transformer model on transaction sequences built in house for Plaid's own products

technical_complexity.rationale: Training transformers from scratch on tens of billions of events and deploying inside customer VPCs under SOC 2 is hard for two people; the company claims a 112 percent PR-AUC gain at one fintech (self-reported).

defensibility.rationale: Models are customer owned and the method is published research, so the edge is execution and integration depth.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large players built in-house transaction models (Plaid, and Mastercard's Large Transaction Model announced at GTC 2026 per a search summary); no acquisition of Lyon found.

market_need_then: Banks and fintechs spend heavily on fraud and credit models; transaction foundation models were a visible 2025 to 2026 theme in industry articles (Thoughtworks, Fintech Wrap Up).

identity.logo: not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, data ownership focused: Your data. Your cloud. Your Intelligence.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a common city name with heavy search collision; no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Lyon is a two person Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. The thesis matches a real industry trend, and the claimed fintech result is strong, but it competes with in-house efforts at large payments firms and has no confirmed funding beyond YC, so customer concentration and sales cycles with regulated institutions are the main risks.
notes: Funding unverified: Dealroom shows a 125k seed with locked details and Startup Seeker shows 500k raised, so they disagree; neither is recorded as a round. Some pages say Summer 2026; the YC page says Fall 2026. Plaid article date was not visible. Competition is as of the 2026 batch. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition.
